input.content:
chunk_size: 2000 # ms
chunk_overlap: 250 #ms
inbalance_ratio: 1.0 # How much more background samples should be drawn
# Share of the drawn background chunks that comes from the external noise
# pools instead of the labeled recordings. If one source can't fill its
# share (e.g. inbalance_ratio > 1 exhausts the real background chunks),
# the other tops it up.
external_background_ratio: 0.5

augmentation:
  # Target signal-to-noise ratios (dB) for synthetic front_doorbell samples,
  # doorbell = signal, everything else = noise. Spans deeply buried (-15dB)
  # to clearly audible (+15dB) to cover realistic in-the-wild conditions.
  # The -15/-10 levels exist to break a metric ceiling: on the -5..15 sweep
  # every feature variant scored val_f1 1.0 on a ~230-chunk fold, which
  # can't separate them. At -15dB the bell sits ~32x below the noise in
  # power -- hard but still tractable from its narrowband harmonics, where
  # -20dB would be closer to unlabelable. Relies on the bell-like ESC-50
  # classes staying excluded (see noise_pools.esc50): with those in the
  # pool, a noise-dominated mix labeled front_doorbell would teach the
  # model that any bell is the doorbell.
  snrs_db: [-15, -10, -5, 0, 5, 10, 15]
  # How many random noise chunks to pair with each real doorbell chunk, per SNR
  pairs_per_signal_chunk: 2
  # Uniform loudness jitter (+/- dB) applied to each mixed sample so synthetic
  # positives vary in absolute level, not just SNR
  gain_jitter_db: 6
  # External noise pools (prepared by the fetch_noise_* stages). Per mix the
  # pool is chosen uniformly first, then a window within it, so the small
  # labeled-background pool isn't drowned out by these much larger ones.
  external_noise_pools:
    - data/noise/esc50
    - data/noise/demand

noise_pools:
  esc50:
    # Bell-like classes are excluded: at the low end of the SNR sweep the
    # noise dominates the mixture, and a mostly-bell sample labeled
    # front_doorbell would teach the model that other bells are doorbells.
    exclude_categories: [church_bells, clock_alarm]
  demand:
    # Domestic environments plus a hallway — closest to the deployed setting.
    # Other options: OOFFICE, OMEETING, PCAFETER, PRESTO, PSTATION, TBUS,
    # TCAR, TMETRO, SPSQUARE, STRAFFIC, SCAFE, NFIELD, NPARK, NRIVER
    environments: [DKITCHEN, DLIVING, DWASHING, OHALLWAY]

# Which feature representation to build. `type` selects an entry in
# src/features.py, which owns both the transform and the matching chunk
# slicer; the remaining keys are that entry's parameters. Swapping
# representation is `dvc exp run -S feature_extraction.type=...` rather than
# a branch — see the variant table in README/CLAUDE.md.
#
# The default geometry targets ESP32-S3 inference: the first conv activation
# (n_mels x n_frames x 32) is what has to fit in SRAM, and 40x100 lands at
# ~125 KB int8 (internal SRAM) vs ~1 MB for the 129x250 STFT variant.
# hop_length 320 = 20 ms, so a 2000 ms chunk is exactly 100 frames.
#
# features_dir must be distinct per geometry, so variants can coexist on
# disk. extract_features.py stamps a feature_config.json into it and
# draw_data.py refuses to slice arrays whose stamp disagrees with these
# params, which is the backstop if two configs ever do share a directory.
feature_extraction:
  type: logmel
  features_dir: ./data/features/logmel-40mel-320hop
  n_mels: 40
  n_fft: 512 # 32 ms @ 16 kHz
  hop_length: 320 # 20 ms
  fmin: 50
  fmax: 8000
  log_offset: 1.0e-6

training:
  test_size: 0.2
  # Which model family trains on the chunks: `cnn` (src/train_cnn.py) keeps
  # the 2D (bins, frames) structure, `xgboost` (src/train_xgboost.py)
  # flattens it. yamnet features only work with the xgboost head — its
  # slicer pools the time axis away — and train_model.py enforces that.
  head: cnn

model:
  learning_rate: 0.001
  batch_size: 32
  epochs: 100
  early_stopping_patience: 10
  dropout: 0.3
  # Raw STFT magnitudes span orders of magnitude — log-compress them before
  # normalization (see train_cnn.py). The mfcc and logmel extractors already
  # apply a log, so those variants set this false; flip it to true when
  # running feature_extraction.type=stft.
  log_compress: false
  random_state: 42

# int8 TFLite export for the ESP32-S3. Runs for every variant so candidates
# are ranked after quantization, not before; non-cnn heads record a skip.
export:
  # Chunks drawn from the training fold to calibrate activation ranges
  representative_samples: 500
  # Hard gate: fail the export if int8 quantization costs more val F1 than
  # this. Silent quantization collapse is the most likely way a variant
  # produces a model that looks fine offline and does not work on device.
  max_f1_drop: 0.01

-  # MFCCs are already log-domain; raw STFT magnitudes are not (see
-  # train_cnn.py) — flip this on the spectrogram branch
+  # Raw STFT magnitudes span orders of magnitude — log-compress them before
+  # normalization (see train_cnn.py). The mfcc and logmel extractors already
+  # apply a log, so those variants set this false; flip it to true when
+# int8 TFLite export for the ESP32-S3. Runs for every variant so candidates
+# are ranked after quantization, not before; non-cnn heads record a skip.
+  # Chunks drawn from the training fold to calibrate activation ranges
+  # Hard gate: fail the export if int8 quantization costs more val F1 than
+  # this. Silent quantization collapse is the most likely way a variant
+  # produces a model that looks fine offline and does not work on device.

toolUseResult.originalFile:
chunk_size: 2000 # ms
chunk_overlap: 250 #ms
inbalance_ratio: 1.0 # How much more background samples should be drawn
# Share of the drawn background chunks that comes from the external noise
# pools instead of the labeled recordings. If one source can't fill its
# share (e.g. inbalance_ratio > 1 exhausts the real background chunks),
# the other tops it up.
external_background_ratio: 0.5

augmentation:
  # Target signal-to-noise ratios (dB) for synthetic front_doorbell samples,
  # doorbell = signal, everything else = noise. Spans deeply buried (-15dB)
  # to clearly audible (+15dB) to cover realistic in-the-wild conditions.
  # The -15/-10 levels exist to break a metric ceiling: on the -5..15 sweep
  # every feature variant scored val_f1 1.0 on a ~230-chunk fold, which
  # can't separate them. At -15dB the bell sits ~32x below the noise in
  # power -- hard but still tractable from its narrowband harmonics, where
  # -20dB would be closer to unlabelable. Relies on the bell-like ESC-50
  # classes staying excluded (see noise_pools.esc50): with those in the
  # pool, a noise-dominated mix labeled front_doorbell would teach the
  # model that any bell is the doorbell.
  snrs_db: [-15, -10, -5, 0, 5, 10, 15]
  # How many random noise chunks to pair with each real doorbell chunk, per SNR
  pairs_per_signal_chunk: 2
  # Uniform loudness jitter (+/- dB) applied to each mixed sample so synthetic
  # positives vary in absolute level, not just SNR
  gain_jitter_db: 6
  # External noise pools (prepared by the fetch_noise_* stages). Per mix the
  # pool is chosen uniformly first, then a window within it, so the small
  # labeled-background pool isn't drowned out by these much larger ones.
  external_noise_pools:
    - data/noise/esc50
    - data/noise/demand

noise_pools:
  esc50:
    # Bell-like classes are excluded: at the low end of the SNR sweep the
    # noise dominates the mixture, and a mostly-bell sample labeled
    # front_doorbell would teach the model that other bells are doorbells.
    exclude_categories: [church_bells, clock_alarm]
  demand:
    # Domestic environments plus a hallway — closest to the deployed setting.
    # Other options: OOFFICE, OMEETING, PCAFETER, PRESTO, PSTATION, TBUS,
    # TCAR, TMETRO, SPSQUARE, STRAFFIC, SCAFE, NFIELD, NPARK, NRIVER
    environments: [DKITCHEN, DLIVING, DWASHING, OHALLWAY]

# Log-mel filterbank energies instead of MFCCs (this branch's experiment).
# Geometry deliberately mirrors the cnn-mfcc baseline -- same n_fft, same
# librosa-default hop of 512 (62 frames per 2000 ms chunk), same number of
# bands as n_mfcc was -- so the only thing that changes between the two runs
# is the missing DCT. Bump n_mels to widen the filterbank afterwards.
feature_extraction:
  type: logmel
  features_dir: ./data/logmel_data
  n_mels: 13
  n_fft: 512 # 32 ms @ 16 kHz
  hop_length: 512 # librosa.feature.mfcc default, kept for chunk-geometry parity
  # librosa.feature.mfcc's own mel filterbank defaults: full 0..sr/2 band
  fmin: 0
  fmax: null
  log_offset: 1.0e-6

training:
  test_size: 0.2

model:
  learning_rate: 0.001
  batch_size: 32
  epochs: 100
  early_stopping_patience: 10
  dropout: 0.3
  # MFCCs are already log-domain; raw STFT magnitudes are not (see
  # train_cnn.py) — flip this on the spectrogram branch
  log_compress: false
  random_state: 42

stages:

  extract_data_quality:
    cmd: python ./src/extract_data_quality.py
    deps:
    - data/annotation_per_row_data.csv

    - data/data_quality/sample_based_quality.json
    - data/data_quality/samples_per_label.csv

  fetch_noise_esc50:
    cmd: python src/fetch_noise_esc50.py
    deps:
    - src/fetch_noise_esc50.py
    - src/noise_pool.py
    params:
    - noise_pools.esc50
    outs:
    - data/noise/esc50

  fetch_noise_demand:
    cmd: python src/fetch_noise_demand.py
    deps:
    - src/fetch_noise_demand.py
    - src/noise_pool.py
    params:
    - noise_pools.demand
    outs:
    - data/noise/demand

  augmentation:
    cmd: python src/augment_data.py
    deps:
    - data/audio
    - data/noise/esc50
    - data/noise/demand
    - data/annotation_per_row_data.csv
    - src/augment_data.py
    params:
    - chunk_size
    - chunk_overlap
    - augmentation

    - data/augmented_audio
    - data/augmented_annotations.csv

  # Which chunks make up the dataset. Deliberately free of any
  # feature_extraction param: every representation trains on the same chunks
  # in the same order, and sweeping features reuses this stage's cache.
  select_chunks:
    cmd: python src/select_chunks.py
    deps:
    - data/annotation_per_row_data.csv
    - data/augmented_annotations.csv
    - data/audio
    - data/augmented_audio
    - data/noise/esc50
    - data/noise/demand
    - src/select_chunks.py
    - src/audio_sources.py
    - src/dataqualityutils.py
    - src/paths.py
    params:
    - chunk_size
    - chunk_overlap
    - inbalance_ratio

    - augmentation.external_noise_pools
    outs:
    - data/chunk_manifest.csv
    - data/data_quality/chunks_per_label.csv
    - data/data_quality/chunk_balanced_quality.json

  # Downstream of select_chunks, so only the files a chunk references get

  extract_features:
    cmd: python src/extract_features.py
    deps:
    - data/chunk_manifest.csv
    - data/audio
    - data/augmented_audio
    - data/noise/esc50
    - data/noise/demand
    - src/extract_features.py
    - src/features.py
    - src/audio_sources.py
    - src/paths.py
    params:
    - feature_extraction
    outs:
    - ${feature_extraction.features_dir}

  draw_data:
    cmd: python src/draw_data.py
    deps:
    - data/chunk_manifest.csv
    - ${feature_extraction.features_dir}
    - src/draw_data.py
    - src/features.py
    - src/paths.py
    params:
    - feature_extraction
    outs:
    - data/balanced_data.h5

  train_model:
    cmd: python src/train_model.py
    deps:
    - data/balanced_data.h5
    - data/data_quality/sample_based_quality.json
    - data/data_quality/samples_per_label.csv
    - data/data_quality/chunk_balanced_quality.json
    - data/data_quality/chunks_per_label.csv
    - src/train_model.py
    - src/train_cnn.py
    - src/train_xgboost.py
    - src/features.py
    - src/paths.py
    params:
    - model
    - training
    outs:
    - models/trained

  # In the default DAG so candidates are ranked on their post-quantization
  # score; non-cnn heads write a skip marker instead of a model.
  export_model:
    cmd: python src/export_tflite.py
    deps:
    - data/balanced_data.h5
    - models/trained
    - src/export_tflite.py
    - src/train_cnn.py
    - src/train_xgboost.py
    - src/paths.py
    params:
    - export
    - model.log_compress
    - model.random_state
    - training
    outs:
    - models/export
    metrics:
    - models/tflite_metrics.json:
        cache: false

metrics:
- data/data_quality/sample_based_quality.json
- data/data_quality/chunk_balanced_quality.json
plots:
- number of samples vs label:
    template: bar_horizontal_sorted
    x: '0'
    y:
      data/data_quality/samples_per_label.csv: label
params:
- params.yaml

    def test_both_short_returns_what_exists(self):
        self.assertEqual(split_background_draw(100, 0.5, 30, 40), (30, 40))

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
            pool_dir = Path(tmp_dir) / "esc50"
            pool_dir.mkdir()
            samples = np.zeros(16000, dtype=np.int16)
            sf.write(pool_dir / "a.wav", samples, 16000)
            sf.write(pool_dir / "b.wav", samples, 16000)

            rows = external_background_rows([str(pool_dir)])

            self.assertEqual(len(rows), 2)
            self.assertTrue((rows["label"] == "background").all())
            self.assertTrue((rows["noise_pool"] == "esc50").all())
            self.assertTrue((rows["start"] == 0.0).all())
            # no end time: the real file duration is filled in downstream,
            # like tag-only real background annotations
            self.assertTrue(rows["end"].isna().all())
            self.assertEqual(list(rows["audio_file_name"]), ["a.wav", "b.wav"])

    def test_empty_pool_list(self):
        self.assertEqual(len(external_background_rows([])), 0)


def _annotation(name, label, start, end, noise_pool=np.nan):
    return {
        "annotation_id": f"{name}-{label}",
        "file_id": name,
        "start": start,
        "end": end,
        "label": label,
        "audio_file_name": f"{name}.wav",
        "remote_audio_path": "",
        "noise_pool": noise_pool,
        "split_group": f"{name}.wav",
    }

    def test_sliding_window_respects_overlap(self):
        annotations = pd.DataFrame([_annotation("rec", "front_doorbell", 0.0, 10.0)])
        chunks = cut_into_chunks(annotations, chunk_size=2000, chunk_overlap=250)
        starts = list(chunks["chunk_start"])
        self.assertEqual(starts[:3], [0, 250, 500])
        # last window must end inside the annotation
        self.assertLess(chunks["chunk_end"].max(), 10_000)

    def test_annotation_shorter_than_chunk_yields_nothing(self):
        annotations = pd.DataFrame([_annotation("blip", "front_doorbell", 0.0, 1.5)])
        self.assertEqual(len(cut_into_chunks(annotations, 2000, 250)), 0)

    def test_chunk_end_is_chunk_size_past_start(self):
        annotations = pd.DataFrame([_annotation("rec", "background", 0.0, 6.0)])
        chunks = cut_into_chunks(annotations, chunk_size=2000, chunk_overlap=500)
        self.assertTrue(((chunks["chunk_end"] - chunks["chunk_start"]) == 2000).all())

    def setUp(self):
        self.params = {"inbalance_ratio": 1.0, "external_background_ratio": 0.5}
        annotations = pd.DataFrame(
            [
                _annotation("bell", "front_doorbell", 0.0, 30.0),
                _annotation("room", "background", 0.0, 60.0),
                _annotation("esc", "background", 0.0, 60.0, noise_pool="esc50"),
            ]
        )
        self.chunks = cut_into_chunks(annotations, 2000, 250)

    def test_background_matches_positive_count(self):
        balanced = balance_chunks(self.chunks, self.params)
        counts = balanced.groupby("label").size()
        self.assertEqual(counts["background"], counts["front_doorbell"])

    def test_background_split_between_real_and_external(self):
        balanced = balance_chunks(self.chunks, self.params)
        background = balanced[balanced["label"] == "background"]
        n_external = background["noise_pool"].notna().sum()
        n_real = background["noise_pool"].isna().sum()
        self.assertEqual(n_real, n_external)

    def test_selection_is_deterministic(self):
        """Feature variants re-run this stage independently; identical input
        must give an identical manifest or the comparison is meaningless."""
        first = balance_chunks(self.chunks, self.params)
        second = balance_chunks(self.chunks, self.params)
        pd.testing.assert_frame_equal(first, second)

    def test_rows_are_shuffled_not_grouped_by_label(self):
        balanced = balance_chunks(self.chunks, self.params)
        labels = list(balanced["label"])
        transitions = sum(a != b for a, b in zip(labels, labels[1:]))
        self.assertGreater(transitions, len(labels) // 10)

    def test_inbalance_ratio_scales_background(self):
        balanced = balance_chunks(
            self.chunks, {**self.params, "inbalance_ratio": 0.5}
        )
        counts = balanced.groupby("label").size()
        self.assertEqual(counts["background"], counts["front_doorbell"] // 2)


class TestHeadCompatibility(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_cnn_rejects_time_pooled_features(self):
        from src.train_model import check_compatible

        with self.assertRaises(SystemExit) as ctx:

        self.assertIn("xgboost", str(ctx.exception))

    def test_xgboost_accepts_any_feature_type(self):
        from src.train_model import check_compatible

        for feature_type in ["mfcc", "logmel", "stft", "yamnet"]:
            with self.subTest(feature_type):
                check_compatible("xgboost", feature_type)

    def test_unknown_head_is_reported(self):
        from src.train_model import check_compatible

        with self.assertRaises(SystemExit) as ctx:
            check_compatible("randomforest", "logmel")
        self.assertIn("randomforest", str(ctx.exception))

10	to train an XGBoost bell classifier.
11	
12	## ML Data Pipeline (DVC)
13	
14	`uv run dvc repro` runs the full chain:
15	`fetch_labeled_data` (Label Studio CSV export) → `convert_labeled_data` →
16	`download_audio` (S3) → `extract_data_quality` / `augmentation` (SNR-mixed synthetic
17	`front_doorbell` samples) → `extract_features` (MFCC, real + augmented audio) →
18	`draw_data` (chunking + balancing) → `train_model` (XGBoost + MLflow).
19	
20	- **Storage layout:** bucket `doorbell-detector` on MinIO — `raw/` (audio, Label Studio
21	  source storage), `annotations/` (Label Studio target-storage sync, backup only),
22	  `dvc/` (DVC remote, configured in `.dvc/config`).
23	- **Credentials** live in the git-ignored `.env`: `LABEL_STUDIO_URL`,
24	  `LABEL_STUDIO_API_KEY`, `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`,
25	  `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`, `MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME`,
26	  `MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD`. Source it before `dvc repro`/`dvc push`.
27	- **Experiment tracking:** `train_xgboost.py` logs params/metrics/model/confusion-matrix
28	  to MLflow (experiment `doorbell-detector`) at `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` — a self-hosted
29	  server (`https://mlflow.saadeh.dev`), not managed from this repo. `dvc metrics
30	  show`/`dvc plots diff` no longer cover training metrics; check the MLflow UI instead.
31	  Runs are named `xgboost-<feature_type>-<git_branch>` (feature type auto-detected from
32	  the `*_features` column in `balanced_data.h5`) and log `balanced_data_md5` — the md5
33	  DVC records for the dataset — so every run traces to an exact, `dvc pull`-able
34	  dataset version.
35	- **Label Studio auth** is a JWT personal access token: `fetch_data.sh` exchanges it
36	  via `/api/token/refresh` for a Bearer token (legacy `Token` header returns 401).
37	- **Incrementality:** `data/audio` is a `persist: true` output — unchanged labels skip
38	  the download stage entirely; changed labels download only missing files and prune
39	  removed ones. Labels are only re-fetched explicitly:
40	  `uv run dvc repro -f fetch_labeled_data && uv run dvc repro`.
41	- **Labeling convention:** bell events get span labels (e.g. `front_doorbell`);
42	  tag-only annotations (doorslam, voice, silence, …) have an empty `label` column in
43	  the export and become full-file `background` rows in the converter. The end time is
44	  filled with the real file duration in `draw_data.py`.
45	- `convert_labeled_data.py` normalizes any Label Studio audio reference (plain
46	  `s3://`, presigned URL, resolver path) to canonical `s3://bucket/key` so presigned
47	  URL churn never dirties the pipeline.
48	- `extract_mfcc_features.py` downmixes to mono — stereo uploads would silently double
49	  the MFCC frame rate and break chunking.
50	- Requires `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` on the host (pydub `mediainfo`).
51	- **Augmentation (`augment_data.py`):** grows the minority `front_doorbell` class by
52	  mixing real doorbell chunks (signal) with real background chunks (noise) via simple
53	  addition at each `augmentation.snrs_db` target SNR (`params.yaml`; `flat_doorbell` is
54	  excluded — too little raw data to seed it). Each signal chunk is paired with
55	  `pairs_per_signal_chunk` random noise chunks per SNR; the noise is circularly
56	  time-shifted and each mix gets ±`gain_jitter_db` uniform loudness jitter. Rows carry
57	  `split_group` = source file of the signal chunk (leakage guard, see training note
58	  below). Output rows carry `end = (chunk_size +
59	  1) / 1000`, 1ms past the real chunk length; this is a deliberate metadata trick so
60	  `draw_data.py`'s sliding-window loop emits exactly one `chunk_start=0` window per
61	  augmented file, reusing the real-annotation chunking path unmodified.
62	- `get_mfcc_features` in `draw_data.py` slices chunks using a **fixed**
63	  `sample_rate/hop_length` frame rate, not `mfccs.shape[1] / file_duration`. The latter
64	  is biased by librosa's constant `+1` frame-count offset — negligible for long real
65	  files (always rounded to the same width) but dominant for exactly `chunk_size`-long
66	  augmented clips (rounded to a different width), which broke `np.vstack` in
67	  `train_xgboost.py` once augmented and real chunks were trained together.
68	- **Train/val split is group-aware** (`train_xgboost.py`): `StratifiedGroupKFold`
69	  grouped by `split_group` (source recording; augmented rows inherit their signal
70	  chunk's source file). A plain random chunk split leaks near-duplicate overlapping
71	  windows and SNR variants across the split and inflates validation metrics.

`uv run dvc repro` runs the full chain:
`fetch_labeled_data` (Label Studio CSV export) → `convert_labeled_data` →
`download_audio` (S3) → `extract_data_quality` / `augmentation` (SNR-mixed synthetic
`front_doorbell` samples) → `extract_features` (MFCC, real + augmented audio) →
`draw_data` (chunking + balancing) → `train_model` (XGBoost + MLflow).

- **Storage layout:** bucket `doorbell-detector` on MinIO — `raw/` (audio, Label Studio
  source storage), `annotations/` (Label Studio target-storage sync, backup only),
  `dvc/` (DVC remote, configured in `.dvc/config`).
- **Credentials** live in the git-ignored `.env`: `LABEL_STUDIO_URL`,
  `LABEL_STUDIO_API_KEY`, `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`,

- **Experiment tracking:** `train_xgboost.py` logs params/metrics/model/confusion-matrix
  to MLflow (experiment `doorbell-detector`) at `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` — a self-hosted
  server (`https://mlflow.saadeh.dev`), not managed from this repo. `dvc metrics
  show`/`dvc plots diff` no longer cover training metrics; check the MLflow UI instead.
  Runs are named `xgboost-<feature_type>-<git_branch>` (feature type auto-detected from
  the `*_features` column in `balanced_data.h5`) and log `balanced_data_md5` — the md5
  DVC records for the dataset — so every run traces to an exact, `dvc pull`-able
  dataset version.
- **Label Studio auth** is a JWT personal access token: `fetch_data.sh` exchanges it
  via `/api/token/refresh` for a Bearer token (legacy `Token` header returns 401).
- **Incrementality:** `data/audio` is a `persist: true` output — unchanged labels skip
  the download stage entirely; changed labels download only missing files and prune

  `uv run dvc repro -f fetch_labeled_data && uv run dvc repro`.
- **Labeling convention:** bell events get span labels (e.g. `front_doorbell`);
  tag-only annotations (doorslam, voice, silence, …) have an empty `label` column in
  the export and become full-file `background` rows in the converter. The end time is
  filled with the real file duration in `draw_data.py`.

  URL churn never dirties the pipeline.

  the MFCC frame rate and break chunking.
- Requires `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` on the host (pydub `mediainfo`).

  mixing real doorbell chunks (signal) with real background chunks (noise) via simple
  addition at each `augmentation.snrs_db` target SNR (`params.yaml`; `flat_doorbell` is
  excluded — too little raw data to seed it). Each signal chunk is paired with

  time-shifted and each mix gets ±`gain_jitter_db` uniform loudness jitter. Rows carry
  `split_group` = source file of the signal chunk (leakage guard, see training note
  below). Output rows carry `end = (chunk_size +

  augmented file, reusing the real-annotation chunking path unmodified.

  `sample_rate/hop_length` frame rate, not `mfccs.shape[1] / file_duration`. The latter

  chunk's source file). A plain random chunk split leaks near-duplicate overlapping
  windows and SNR variants across the split and inflates validation metrics.

# Doorbell Detector — Project Guide

## What This Is

Audio-based doorbell detection system running on a Raspberry Pi. The project has two
main modes: an ML-based collector (`data_collection/data_collector.py`) and a
pattern-matching detector (`data_collection/detector.py`), deployed as a systemd
service. Alongside the Pi scripts lives a DVC-managed ML pipeline (`src/`, `dvc.yaml`)
that pulls labels from Label Studio and raw audio from a self-hosted MinIO S3 bucket
to train an XGBoost bell classifier.

## ML Data Pipeline (DVC)

`uv run dvc repro` runs the full chain:
`fetch_labeled_data` (Label Studio CSV export) → `convert_labeled_data` →
`download_audio` (S3) → `extract_data_quality` / `augmentation` (SNR-mixed synthetic
`front_doorbell` samples) → `extract_features` (MFCC, real + augmented audio) →
`draw_data` (chunking + balancing) → `train_model` (XGBoost + MLflow).

- **Storage layout:** bucket `doorbell-detector` on MinIO — `raw/` (audio, Label Studio
  source storage), `annotations/` (Label Studio target-storage sync, backup only),
  `dvc/` (DVC remote, configured in `.dvc/config`).
- **Credentials** live in the git-ignored `.env`: `LABEL_STUDIO_URL`,
  `LABEL_STUDIO_API_KEY`, `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`,
  `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`, `MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME`,
  `MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD`. Source it before `dvc repro`/`dvc push`.
- **Experiment tracking:** `train_xgboost.py` logs params/metrics/model/confusion-matrix
  to MLflow (experiment `doorbell-detector`) at `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` — a self-hosted
  server (`https://mlflow.saadeh.dev`), not managed from this repo. `dvc metrics
  show`/`dvc plots diff` no longer cover training metrics; check the MLflow UI instead.
  Runs are named `xgboost-<feature_type>-<git_branch>` (feature type auto-detected from
  the `*_features` column in `balanced_data.h5`) and log `balanced_data_md5` — the md5
  DVC records for the dataset — so every run traces to an exact, `dvc pull`-able
  dataset version.
- **Label Studio auth** is a JWT personal access token: `fetch_data.sh` exchanges it
  via `/api/token/refresh` for a Bearer token (legacy `Token` header returns 401).
- **Incrementality:** `data/audio` is a `persist: true` output — unchanged labels skip
  the download stage entirely; changed labels download only missing files and prune
  removed ones. Labels are only re-fetched explicitly:
  `uv run dvc repro -f fetch_labeled_data && uv run dvc repro`.
- **Labeling convention:** bell events get span labels (e.g. `front_doorbell`);
  tag-only annotations (doorslam, voice, silence, …) have an empty `label` column in
  the export and become full-file `background` rows in the converter. The end time is
  filled with the real file duration in `draw_data.py`.
- `convert_labeled_data.py` normalizes any Label Studio audio reference (plain
  `s3://`, presigned URL, resolver path) to canonical `s3://bucket/key` so presigned
  URL churn never dirties the pipeline.
- `extract_mfcc_features.py` downmixes to mono — stereo uploads would silently double
  the MFCC frame rate and break chunking.
- Requires `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` on the host (pydub `mediainfo`).
- **Augmentation (`augment_data.py`):** grows the minority `front_doorbell` class by
  mixing real doorbell chunks (signal) with real background chunks (noise) via simple
  addition at each `augmentation.snrs_db` target SNR (`params.yaml`; `flat_doorbell` is
  excluded — too little raw data to seed it). Each signal chunk is paired with
  `pairs_per_signal_chunk` random noise chunks per SNR; the noise is circularly
  time-shifted and each mix gets ±`gain_jitter_db` uniform loudness jitter. Rows carry
  `split_group` = source file of the signal chunk (leakage guard, see training note
  below). Output rows carry `end = (chunk_size +
  1) / 1000`, 1ms past the real chunk length; this is a deliberate metadata trick so
  `draw_data.py`'s sliding-window loop emits exactly one `chunk_start=0` window per
  augmented file, reusing the real-annotation chunking path unmodified.
- `get_mfcc_features` in `draw_data.py` slices chunks using a **fixed**
  `sample_rate/hop_length` frame rate, not `mfccs.shape[1] / file_duration`. The latter
  is biased by librosa's constant `+1` frame-count offset — negligible for long real
  files (always rounded to the same width) but dominant for exactly `chunk_size`-long
  augmented clips (rounded to a different width), which broke `np.vstack` in
  `train_xgboost.py` once augmented and real chunks were trained together.
- **Train/val split is group-aware** (`train_xgboost.py`): `StratifiedGroupKFold`
  grouped by `split_group` (source recording; augmented rows inherit their signal
  chunk's source file). A plain random chunk split leaks near-duplicate overlapping
  windows and SNR variants across the split and inflates validation metrics.
  `training.test_size` maps to the fold fraction (1/n_splits); the realized fraction
  is logged to MLflow as `realized_test_fraction`.

## GSD Workflow

This project uses [Get Shit Done](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/gsd) for structured
planning and execution.

**Status:** v1.0 milestone complete — all 3 phases shipped 2026-06-25. Post-milestone
hardening (MQTT trigger fixes, audio drop fixes, template auto-trim) has continued
directly on `detector.py` outside the phase structure.
**Planning docs:** `.planning/`

### Workflow commands

```
/gsd-progress          # Check status, start next milestone
/gsd-new-milestone     # Scope v2 work (see Deferred Items in .planning/STATE.md)
```

### Phases (all complete)

1. **Script Foundation** — CLI, audio device setup, template loading, error handling
2. **Detection & Notification** — Cross-correlation loop, threshold/cooldown, MQTT publish
3. **Data Collection** — `--save` flag, ring buffer clips, timestamped WAV output

v2 deferred items (not yet scoped): multiple template files, FFT frequency-domain
matching, GPIO button trigger, Prometheus metrics/health endpoint.

## Codebase Notes

- Audio constants: 16 kHz, mono, int16 — never change without updating all scripts
- Device name `seeed-2mic-voicecard` is hardcoded in data_collector.py; detector.py has a `--device-name` override
- MQTT password is passed as a CLI arg (visible in `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`) — known limitation, not a bug to fix here
- `ssl.PROTOCOL_TLS` is deprecated in Python 3.12+ — present in both scripts, carry forward as-is
- `src/deploy.sh` references the old path `src/data_collector.py` (file moved) — broken, out of scope for this work
- Oversized templates are auto-trimmed to their most energetic window (see `0b3163a`)
- Cross-correlation is slow enough to drop audio in saved clips if not handled carefully (see `c8c2788`)
- Root `requirements.txt` was removed — `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock` is the single source
  of pipeline dependencies (`data_collection/requirements.txt` remains for the Pi)
- All 44 tests pass; run with `PYTHONPATH=./src:. uv run pytest tests/`

## Key Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `data_collection/data_collector.py` | Existing collector: ML + MQTT + GPIO triggers |
| `data_collection/detector.py` | Pattern-matching detector: cross-correlation, MQTT notify, `--save` clip capture |
| `data_collection/systemd/doorbell-detector.service` | systemd unit for running detector.py on the Pi |
| `data_collection/systemd/doorbell-detector.env` | Env file consumed by the systemd unit (MQTT creds, buffer/threshold config) |
| `data_collection/requirements.txt` | Pi runtime dependencies |
| `dvc.yaml` / `dvc.lock` | ML pipeline stage definitions and lock state |
| `src/fetch_data.sh` | Label Studio CSV export (JWT token exchange) |
| `src/convert_labeled_data.py` | Export → annotation-per-row CSV; URI normalization; tag-only → background |
| `src/download_audio.py` | Incremental S3 audio download (boto3) with pruning |
| `src/augment_data.py` | SNR-mixed synthetic `front_doorbell` samples (signal+noise addition) |
| `src/extract_mfcc_features.py` | MFCC extraction (mono-downmixed; real + augmented audio) |
| `src/draw_data.py` | Chunking, background balancing → `balanced_data.h5` |
| `src/train_xgboost.py` | XGBoost training with MLflow tracking |
| `params.yaml` | ML pipeline parameters (not used by detector) |
| `.env` | Git-ignored credentials for Label Studio + MinIO + MLflow |
| `.planning/REQUIREMENTS.md` | 15 v1 requirements with REQ-IDs |
| `.planning/ROADMAP.md` | 3-phase roadmap (all complete) |
| `.planning/STATE.md` | Milestone status and deferred v2 items |

## Commands

This project uses uv for dependency and venv management, so use `uv` to run python
commands.

```
set -a; source .env; set +a       # load credentials first
uv run dvc repro                  # run/refresh the pipeline (labels NOT re-fetched)
uv run dvc repro -f fetch_labeled_data && uv run dvc repro   # refresh labels too
uv run dvc push                   # push data/model versions to MinIO
PYTHONPATH=./src:. uv run pytest tests/
```

49	  `MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD`. Source it before `dvc repro`/`dvc push`.
50	- **Experiment tracking:** `train_xgboost.py` logs params/metrics/model/confusion-matrix
51	  to MLflow (experiment `doorbell-detector`) at `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` — a self-hosted
52	  server (`https://mlflow.saadeh.dev`), not managed from this repo. `dvc metrics
53	  show`/`dvc plots diff` no longer cover training metrics; check the MLflow UI instead.
54	  Runs are named `<head>-<feature_type>-<git_branch>` (feature type auto-detected from
55	  the `*_features` column in `balanced_data.h5`) and log `balanced_data_md5` — the md5
56	  DVC records for the dataset — so every run traces to an exact, `dvc pull`-able
57	  dataset version.
58	- **Label Studio auth** is a JWT personal access token: `fetch_data.sh` exchanges it
59	  via `/api/token/refresh` for a Bearer token (legacy `Token` header returns 401).
60	- **Incrementality:** `data/audio` is a `persist: true` output — unchanged labels skip
61	  the download stage entirely; changed labels download only missing files and prune
62	  removed ones. Labels are only re-fetched explicitly:
63	  `uv run dvc repro -f fetch_labeled_data && uv run dvc repro`.
64	- **Labeling convention:** bell events get span labels (e.g. `front_doorbell`);
65	  tag-only annotations (doorslam, voice, silence, …) have an empty `label` column in
66	  the export and become full-file `background` rows in the converter. The end time is
67	  filled with the real file duration in `select_chunks.py`.
68	- `convert_labeled_data.py` normalizes any Label Studio audio reference (plain
69	  `s3://`, presigned URL, resolver path) to canonical `s3://bucket/key` so presigned
70	  URL churn never dirties the pipeline.
71	- `features.py::_load_mono_int16_scale` downmixes to mono — stereo uploads would
72	  silently double the frame rate and break chunking. Audio is kept at int16 amplitude
73	  scale (not [-1, 1]); normalization happens globally at training time.
74	- Requires `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` on the host (pydub `mediainfo`).
75	- **Augmentation (`augment_data.py`):** grows the minority `front_doorbell` class by
76	  mixing real doorbell chunks (signal) with real background chunks (noise) via simple
77	  addition at each `augmentation.snrs_db` target SNR (`params.yaml`; `flat_doorbell` is
78	  excluded — too little raw data to seed it). Each signal chunk is paired with
79	  `pairs_per_signal_chunk` random noise chunks per SNR; the noise is circularly
80	  time-shifted and each mix gets ±`gain_jitter_db` uniform loudness jitter. Rows carry
81	  `split_group` = source file of the signal chunk (leakage guard, see training note
82	  below). Output rows carry `end = (chunk_size +
83	  1) / 1000`, 1ms past the real chunk length; this is a deliberate metadata trick so
84	  `select_chunks.py`'s sliding-window loop emits exactly one `chunk_start=0` window per
85	  augmented file, reusing the real-annotation chunking path unmodified.
86	- `fixed_rate_slice` in `features.py` slices chunks using a **fixed**
87	  `sample_rate/hop_length` frame rate, not `array.shape[1] / file_duration`. The latter
88	  is biased by librosa's constant `+1` frame-count offset — negligible for long real
89	  files (always rounded to the same width) but dominant for exactly `chunk_size`-long
90	  augmented clips (rounded to a different width), which broke `np.vstack` in
91	  `train_xgboost.py` once augmented and real chunks were trained together. `yamnet` is
92	  the exception: it mean-pools the covering frames instead, because a 2s augmented clip
93	  yields 3 embedding frames where a 2s slice of a long file yields 4. That pooling
94	  removes the time axis, so `yamnet` only works with the `xgboost` head —
95	  `train_model.py` enforces it.
96	- **Train/val split is group-aware** (`prepare_split` in `train_cnn.py`): `StratifiedGroupKFold`
97	  grouped by `split_group` (source recording; augmented rows inherit their signal
98	  chunk's source file). A plain random chunk split leaks near-duplicate overlapping
99	  windows and SNR variants across the split and inflates validation metrics.
100	  `training.test_size` maps to the fold fraction (1/n_splits); the realized fraction

cd /home/orchid/projects/doorbell-detector
export PYTHONPATH=./src:.
uv run pytest tests/ -q 2>&1 | tail -3
git add -A
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
one parameterized pipeline instead of one branch per variant

Every experiment branch (cnn-mfcc, cnn-spectrogram, yamnet-features,
stft-spectrogram-features, cnn-logmel, esp32-logmel) carried an identical
10-stage DAG differing only in two commands: which extract_*_features.py ran
and which train_*.py ran. Those four extractor scripts were ~90% the same
driver around a ~10-line transform, each paired with a hand-edited slicer
inside its branch's draw_data.py.

Collapse that into parameters:

* src/features.py is a registry keyed by feature_extraction.type, and each
  entry owns both the transform and the matching chunk slicer -- the two
  halves that previously drifted apart across branches. yamnet declares
  keeps_time_axis=False because its slicer pools; train_model.py rejects the
  cnn head for it rather than failing on a shape mismatch later.
* src/train_model.py dispatches on training.head, so the stage cmd is static
  and a variant is `dvc exp run -S`.
* dvc.yaml interpolates ${feature_extraction.features_dir}, so variants keep
  separate feature directories.

Split select_chunks out of draw_data. Sampling now happens before feature
extraction, which means extract_features touches only the 1205 files the
manifest references instead of all 2801 -- the discarded majority was the
external noise pool, ~500 MB of it on the STFT variant. It also makes the
sampling feature-independent, so every variant trains on identical chunks
from one cached stage. Verified byte-identical: the manifest reproduces the
previous balanced_data.h5 row for row, in order.

Add a feature_config.json sidecar that extract_features stamps and draw_data
verifies. This is the guard for the failure behind data/logmel_data.esp32bak,
where two branches wrote 13x512 and 40x320 arrays into one directory name and
nothing noticed until several stages later.

Promote export_model into the default DAG so candidates are ranked on their
post-quantization score, not their float32 one; non-cnn heads write a skip
marker. Model outputs move to models/trained and models/export so each stage
has one static directory out.

Tests go from 44 to 94.

Still training — the STFT CNN runs on 129×250 inputs, ~6× the tensor of the 40×100 variants, so it's the slow one. The `| tail` in my invocation is buffering its output, but MLflow shows `cnn-stft-HEAD` started and `train_model` is live.

Meanwhile the picture from MLflow is already decisive on the comparability question:

| Run | chunks | input | val F1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `xgboost-mfcc-main` | 1298 | flat | 0.9919 |
| `cnn-mfcc-cnn-mfcc` | 1298 | 13×62 | 0.9913 |
| `cnn-stft-cnn-spectrogram` | 1298 | 129×250 | 0.9826 |
| `xgboost-yamnet-yamnet-features` | 1298 | flat | 0.9956 |
| `cnn-logmel-esp32-logmel` | **1298** | 40×100 | 1.0000 |
| `cnn-logmel` (13-band, new sweep) | **1770** | 13×62 | 0.9973 |
| `cnn-logmel-unified-pipeline` | **1770** | 40×100 | 1.0000 |
| `cnn-mfcc-HEAD` (unified) | **1770** | 40×100 | 1.0000 |

Every branch result was on 1298 chunks; the -15 dB sweep produces 1770. The old leaderboard and the new one never shared a dataset — exactly what the lock hashes predicted.

I'll report once STFT and YAMNet land.

content.subject: Port esp32-logmel refactors forward
content.description: Bring load_dataset/prepare_split extraction in train_cnn.py, the accuracy metric in train_xgboost.py, and export_tflite.py onto the unified branch.

content.subject: Split sampling out into select_chunks stage

content.subject: Unify the four feature extractors
content.description: One src/extract_features.py dispatching on feature_extraction.type (mfcc/logmel/stft/yamnet), manifest-driven so only referenced files get extracted, writing a feature_config.json sidecar.

content.subject: Rewrite draw_data as manifest slicer with config guard
content.description: draw_data.py consumes chunk_manifest.csv + features dir, verifies the sidecar matches params, emits balanced_data.h5.

content.subject: Add train_model head dispatcher and rewire dvc.yaml
content.description: src/train_model.py dispatching on training.head; new DAG with ${} param interpolation, export_model promoted and gated.

content.subject: Update and extend the test suite
content.description: Port feature_extraction/logmel tests onto the unified extractor, add tests for select_chunks sampling parity and the config guard. All tests must pass.

content.subject: Re-run all feature variants on the -15dB sweep
content.description: Run the matrix (mfcc/logmel/stft/yamnet x cnn) on the current augmentation to restore a valid leaderboard in MLflow.

cd /home/orchid/projects/doorbell-detector
git add pyproject.toml uv.lock
git checkout -- dvc.lock models/tflite_metrics.json data/features/.gitignore 2>/dev/null
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
one parameterized pipeline instead of one branch per variant

Every experiment branch (cnn-mfcc, cnn-spectrogram, yamnet-features,
stft-spectrogram-features, cnn-logmel, esp32-logmel) carried an identical
10-stage DAG differing only in two commands: which extract_*_features.py ran
and which train_*.py ran. Those four extractor scripts were ~90% the same
driver around a ~10-line transform, each paired with a hand-edited slicer
inside its branch's draw_data.py.

Collapse that into parameters:

* src/features.py is a registry keyed by feature_extraction.type, and each
  entry owns both the transform and the matching chunk slicer -- the two
  halves that previously drifted apart across branches. yamnet declares
  keeps_time_axis=False because its slicer pools; train_model.py rejects the
  cnn head for it rather than failing on a shape mismatch later.
* src/train_model.py dispatches on training.head, so the stage cmd is static
  and a variant is `dvc exp run -S`.
* dvc.yaml interpolates ${feature_extraction.features_dir}, so variants keep
  separate feature directories.

Split select_chunks out of draw_data. Sampling now happens before feature
extraction, which means extract_features touches only the 1205 files the
manifest references instead of all 2801 -- the discarded majority was the
external noise pool, ~500 MB of it on the STFT variant. It also makes the
sampling feature-independent, so every variant trains on identical chunks
from one cached stage. Verified byte-identical: the manifest reproduces the
previous balanced_data.h5 row for row, in order.

Add a feature_config.json sidecar that extract_features stamps and draw_data
verifies. This is the guard for the failure behind data/logmel_data.esp32bak,
where two branches wrote 13x512 and 40x320 arrays into one directory name and
nothing noticed until several stages later.

Promote export_model into the default DAG so candidates are ranked on their
post-quantization score, not their float32 one; non-cnn heads write a skip
marker. Model outputs move to models/trained and models/export so each stage
has one static directory out.

tensorflow-hub joins the dependencies: it only ever existed on the
yamnet-features branch, so the yamnet variant could not run anywhere else.

Also gitignore data/stft_data and data/features -- leftover feature caches
from the branch era were not covered.

Tests go from 44 to 94.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.text: The killed `dvc exp run` had staged its mutated `params.yaml`, and my `--soft` reset preserved that index — so the commit captured `type: yamnet` as the repo default. Fixing and amending:

input.command:
cd /home/orchid/projects/doorbell-detector
grep -n "n_mfcc\|^  type:\|features_dir:\|^  head:\|log_compress:" params.yaml
python3 -c "
import pathlib
p=pathlib.Path('params.yaml'); s=p.read_text()
s=s.replace('  type: yamnet\n  features_dir: ./data/features/yamnet\n','  type: logmel\n  features_dir: ./data/features/logmel-40mel-320hop\n')
s=s.replace('  head: xgboost\n','  head: cnn\n')
p.write_text(s)"
echo "--- after ---"; grep -n "^  type:\|features_dir:\|^  head:\|log_compress:\|n_mfcc" params.yaml

content.text:
YAMNet running in an isolated temp workspace. Meanwhile — an honest note on two mistakes I made and fixed:

**I committed 769 MB of data into git.** I used `git add -A`, which swept in `data/stft_data/` — a leftover feature cache from the `stft-spectrogram-features` branch that `data/.gitignore` never covered (it lists `mfcc_data`, `logmel_data`, but not `stft_data`). `.git` went 17 MB → 786 MB. Rewritten out, refs cleaned, `.git` back to **17 MB**. `/stft_data` and `/features` are now gitignored.

**`dvc exp run` left HEAD detached and staged its mutated `params.yaml`.** So my "clean" recommit landed off-branch, and captured `type: yamnet, head: xgboost` as the repo default. Both fixed: branch reattached at the good commit, default restored to `logmel`/`cnn`, amended. Worktree clean, 94 tests pass.

Worth knowing for the future: `dvc exp run` mutates `params.yaml` **and the index** in the workspace. `--temp` avoids both, which is why YAMNet is running that way now.

content.text: Confirmed regression I introduced: one `model:` block feeding both heads, so XGBoost got the CNN's `learning_rate: 0.001` (with XGBoost's default 100 estimators) instead of `n_estimators: 25, learning_rate: 0.1` — plus junk kwargs like `dropout`. It barely learned. Fixing properly:

input.command:
cd /home/orchid/projects/doorbell-detector
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib

# 1. params.yaml: per-head model blocks; random_state and log_compress move out
p = pathlib.Path("params.yaml"); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace("""training:
  test_size: 0.2""", """training:
  test_size: 0.2
  # Seed for the split, and for whichever head trains on it
  random_state: 42""")
old_model = s[s.index("\nmodel:"):s.index("\n# int8 TFLite export")]
s = s.replace(old_model, """
# Per-head hyperparameters. Nested because the two heads share nothing: a
# flat block meant XGBoost silently received the CNN's learning_rate (0.001,
# against xgboost's default 100 estimators) plus dropout/epochs as unknown
# kwargs, and barely learned at all.
model:
  cnn:
    learning_rate: 0.001
    batch_size: 32
    epochs: 100
    early_stopping_patience: 10
    dropout: 0.3
  xgboost:
    n_estimators: 25
    max_depth: 6
    learning_rate: 0.1
    eval_metric: ["logloss", "error"]
""")
p.write_text(s)

# 2. features.py: log-compression becomes a property of the representation
p = pathlib.Path("src/features.py"); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace("""    # A CNN head needs the (bins, frames) structure; yamnet_slice pools the
    # time axis away and returns a 1D embedding, which only the flattening
    # tree head can consume.
    keeps_time_axis: bool = True""",
"""    # A CNN head needs the (bins, frames) structure; yamnet_slice pools the
    # time axis away and returns a 1D embedding, which only the flattening
    # tree head can consume.
    keeps_time_axis: bool = True
    # Whether the trainer must log-compress before normalizing. A property of
    # the representation, not of the model: raw STFT magnitudes span orders of
    # magnitude, while mfcc/logmel already had a log applied by the extractor.
    # Previously a params.yaml flag with a "flip this on the spectrogram
    # branch" comment -- exactly the kind of thing that silently stays wrong.
    needs_log_compression: bool = False""")
s = s.replace("""        extract=extract_stft,
        slice_chunk=fixed_rate_slice,
    ),""", """        extract=extract_stft,
        slice_chunk=fixed_rate_slice,
        needs_log_compression=True,
    ),""")
p.write_text(s)

# 3. train_cnn.py
p = pathlib.Path("src/train_cnn.py"); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('    model_params = params["model"]\n', '    model_params = params["model"]["cnn"]\n')
s = s.replace('keras.utils.set_random_seed(model_params["random_state"])',
              'keras.utils.set_random_seed(params["training"]["random_state"])')
s = s.replace("""    # Raw STFT magnitudes span orders of magnitude; log-compression makes
    # them tractable for a CNN. MFCC and log-mel branches are already in the
    # log domain (the extractor does it), so they set this false.
    if params["model"]["log_compress"]:
        X = np.log(X + 1e-6)""",
"""    # Whether this is needed is a property of the representation, declared
    # in features.py, not a flag someone has to remember to flip.
    if get_spec(params["feature_extraction"]["type"]).needs_log_compression:
        X = np.log(X + 1e-6)""")
s = s.replace("from paths import DATA_FILE, MODEL_DIR",
              "from features import get_spec\nfrom paths import DATA_FILE, MODEL_DIR")
p.write_text(s)

# 4. train_xgboost.py
p = pathlib.Path("src/train_xgboost.py"); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('    model_params = params["model"]\n', '    model_params = params["model"]["xgboost"]\n')
s = s.replace('model = xgb.XGBClassifier(objective="binary:logistic", **model_params)',
              'model = xgb.XGBClassifier(\n            objective="binary:logistic",\n            random_state=params["training"]["random_state"],\n            **model_params,\n        )')
p.write_text(s)

# 5. export_tflite.py
p = pathlib.Path("src/export_tflite.py"); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('rng = np.random.default_rng(params["model"]["random_state"])',
              'rng = np.random.default_rng(params["training"]["random_state"])')
p.write_text(s)

# 6. dvc.yaml
p = pathlib.Path("dvc.yaml"); s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace("""    params:
    - export
    - model.log_compress
    - model.random_state
    - training""", """    params:
    - export
    - model.cnn
    - training""")
p.write_text(s)
print("patched")
PY
grep -n "model_params = \|random_state" src/train_cnn.py src/train_xgboost.py | head

1	"""One registry for every feature representation the pipeline can build.
2	
3	Previously each representation was its own script on its own branch
4	(extract_mfcc_features.py, extract_stft_features.py, ...), which were ~90%
5	identical boilerplate around a ~10-line transform, and each shipped a
6	matching hand-edited slicer inside draw_data.py. Both halves live here
7	instead, keyed by `feature_extraction.type`, so a variant is a parameter
8	rather than a branch.
9	
10	Each entry owns three things:
11	
12	* `params` -- which keys it reads out of the `feature_extraction` block,
13	  so the sidecar config (and therefore the DVC param hash) contains exactly
14	  what affects the output and nothing else.
15	* `extract` -- file -> (n_bins, n_frames) float array.
16	* `slice_chunk` -- how draw_data.py cuts a [start_ms, end_ms) window out of
17	  that array. This is per-type because it is not always a fixed frame rate
18	  (see yamnet below).
19	"""

21	import json
22	from dataclasses import dataclass
23	from pathlib import Path

33	def _load_mono_int16_scale(file_path: Path | str) -> tuple[np.ndarray, int]:
34	    """Audio as float32 at int16 amplitude scale, downmixed to mono.
35	
36	    Mono matters: stereo files would double the sample count (interleaved)
37	    and break the frames-per-ms assumption the slicers rely on. int16 scale
38	    (rather than [-1, 1]) is kept because every extractor here has always
39	    used it, and normalization happens globally at training time.
40	    """
41	    from pydub import AudioSegment
42	    from pydub.utils import mediainfo
43	
44	    audio = AudioSegment.from_wav(file_path)
45	    info = mediainfo(file_path)
46	    audio = audio.set_channels(1)
47	    samples = np.array(audio.get_array_of_samples(), dtype=np.float32)
48	    return samples, int(info["sample_rate"])

51	def extract_mfcc(file_path, n_mfcc: int, n_fft: int, hop_length: int) -> np.ndarray:
52	    import librosa
53	
54	    samples, sample_rate = _load_mono_int16_scale(file_path)
55	    mfccs = librosa.feature.mfcc(
56	        y=samples, sr=sample_rate, n_mfcc=n_mfcc, n_fft=n_fft, hop_length=hop_length
57	    )
58	    return mfccs.astype(np.float32)

61	def extract_logmel(
62	    file_path,
63	    n_mels: int,
64	    n_fft: int,
65	    hop_length: int,
66	    fmin: int,
67	    fmax: int | None,
68	    log_offset: float,
69	) -> np.ndarray:
70	    """Log-mel filterbank energies -- the MFCC path minus the final DCT.
71	
72	    MFCCs are log-mel energies run through a DCT, which decorrelates the
73	    bins so a tree sees compact, roughly independent features. A CNN does
74	    not want that: it wants the locally correlated structure along the
75	    frequency axis that the DCT destroys.
76	
77	    The log is applied here rather than in the trainer, so params.yaml sets
78	    model.log_compress: false for this type and the .npy files are exactly
79	    what an on-device C frontend has to reproduce.
80	    """
81	    import librosa
82	
83	    samples, sample_rate = _load_mono_int16_scale(file_path)
84	    mel = librosa.feature.melspectrogram(
85	        y=samples,
86	        sr=sample_rate,
87	        n_fft=n_fft,
88	        hop_length=hop_length,
89	        n_mels=n_mels,
90	        fmin=fmin,
91	        fmax=fmax,
92	    )
93	    # log_offset keeps digital-silence frames finite; librosa's power_to_db
94	    # would additionally clip to top_db below the per-file peak, which is a
95	    # per-file operation we don't want ahead of a global normalization.
96	    return np.log(mel + log_offset).astype(np.float32)

99	def extract_stft(file_path, n_fft: int, hop_length: int) -> np.ndarray:
100	    """Raw STFT magnitude. Not log-compressed here -- params.yaml sets
101	    model.log_compress: true for this type so the trainer does it."""

104	    samples, sample_rate = _load_mono_int16_scale(file_path)
105	    _, _, zxx = stft(
106	        samples, fs=sample_rate, nperseg=n_fft, noverlap=n_fft - hop_length

111	def extract_yamnet(file_path, model=None) -> np.ndarray:
112	    """YAMNet (MobileNet-v1 on AudioSet) frame embeddings, (1024, n_frames).
113	
114	    One 1024-dim embedding per 0.48s hop over 0.96s windows of 16kHz mono
115	    audio. `model` is injected by the caller so the TF Hub load happens once
116	    per process rather than once per file.
117	    """
118	    import librosa
119	
120	    if model is None:
121	        model = load_yamnet()
122	    waveform, _ = librosa.load(file_path, sr=SAMPLING_RATE, mono=True)
123	    # zero-pad below one full analysis window, else YAMNet emits no frames
124	    min_samples = int(0.96 * SAMPLING_RATE)
125	    if len(waveform) < min_samples:
126	        waveform = np.pad(waveform, (0, min_samples - len(waveform)))
127	    _, embeddings, _ = model(waveform)
128	    # (n_frames, 1024) -> (1024, n_frames), matching the (bins, time)
129	    # orientation every other type produces
130	    return embeddings.numpy().T.astype(np.float32)

142	    os.environ.setdefault("TFHUB_CACHE_DIR", str(TFHUB_CACHE_DIR))

148	def fixed_rate_slice(array: np.ndarray, start_ms: int, end_ms: int, cfg: dict):
149	    """Cut [start_ms, end_ms) using the extractor's nominal frame rate.
150	
151	    Deliberately NOT a per-file average rate (array.shape[1] / duration):
152	    the frame count carries a constant +1 offset, which is negligible for
153	    long real files (average rate ~= true rate) but dominant for exactly
154	    chunk_size-long augmented clips (average rate skews high). Per-file
155	    rates produced inconsistent chunk widths and broke np.vstack downstream.
156	    """
157	    frames_per_ms = SAMPLING_RATE / cfg["hop_length"] / 1000
158	    start_frame = int(frames_per_ms * start_ms)
159	    # width from the duration, not from end_frame - start_frame, so every
160	    # chunk of a given length comes out the same width
161	    width = int(frames_per_ms * (end_ms - start_ms))
162	    return array[:, start_frame : start_frame + width]

168	def yamnet_slice(array: np.ndarray, start_ms: int, end_ms: int, cfg: dict):
169	    """Cut the covering frames and mean-pool them to one fixed-size vector.
170	
171	    Pooling is what makes the result shape-independent of the frame count:
172	    a 2s augmented clip yields 3 frames (no final partial window) while a 2s
173	    slice of a long file yields 4, and both have to produce the same feature
174	    length for the downstream stack.
175	    """
176	    start_frame = int(start_ms // YAMNET_HOP_MS)
177	    n_frames = max(1, int((end_ms - start_ms) // YAMNET_HOP_MS))
178	    frames = array[:, start_frame : start_frame + n_frames]
179	    if frames.shape[1] == 0:
180	        # chunk starts past the last emitted frame (file-end edge case)
181	        frames = array[:, -1:]
182	    return frames.mean(axis=1)

1	"""Export the trained CNN as a full-integer int8 TFLite model for the ESP32-S3.
2	
3	Two things make this more than a format conversion:
4	
5	1. **Normalization is baked into the graph.** train_cnn.py stores per-mel-bin
6	   mean/std in cnn_normalization.npz and applies them outside the model. Here
7	   they become a Rescaling layer in front of the trained network, so the
8	   firmware's C frontend only has to produce log-mel energies -- everything
9	   after that is the interpreter's job. One less place for train/serve skew.
10	
11	2. **The export is gated on int8 val F1.** Full-integer post-training
12	   quantization can quietly destroy a model that looks fine in float. The
13	   stage recomputes the same leakage-safe split train_cnn.py used, scores the
14	   int8 interpreter on the val fold, and fails if F1 drops by more than
15	   export.max_f1_drop.
16	
17	Outputs models/export/doorbell_int8.tflite (for reference/testing), the
18	equivalent C array in models/export/doorbell_model_data.cc (compiled into
19	the firmware), and models/tflite_metrics.json.
20	
21	The stage runs for every variant in the default DAG, so representations are
22	ranked on their post-quantization score rather than their float32 one. Heads
23	that produce nothing convertible record a skip marker instead (see skip()).
24	"""

27	import json
28	import os
29	import shutil
30	from pathlib import Path
31	
32	import mlflow
33	import numpy as np
34	import tensorflow as tf
35	import yaml
36	from tensorflow import keras

39	from train_cnn import MODEL_PATH, load_dataset, prepare_split

56	def build_export_model(trained: keras.Model, mean: np.ndarray, std: np.ndarray):
57	    """Prepend per-bin normalization so the graph consumes raw log-mel.
58	
59	    mean/std come from normalization_stats() with shape (n_bins, 1, 1), which
60	    broadcasts over the (batch, n_bins, n_frames, 1) input.
61	    """
62	    inputs = keras.Input(shape=trained.input_shape[1:], name="logmel")
63	    x = keras.layers.Rescaling(
64	        scale=(1.0 / std).astype(np.float32),
65	        offset=(-mean / std).astype(np.float32),
66	        name="normalize",
67	    )(inputs)
68	    outputs = trained(x)
69	    return keras.Model(inputs, outputs, name="doorbell_int8_export")

72	def convert_int8(model: keras.Model, representative: np.ndarray) -> bytes:
73	    """Full-integer PTQ. int8 in and out so no float ops remain for TFLM."""
74	    converter = tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.from_keras_model(model)
75	    converter.optimizations = [tf.lite.Optimize.DEFAULT]
76	    converter.target_spec.supported_ops = [tf.lite.OpsSet.TFLITE_BUILTINS_INT8]
77	    converter.inference_input_type = tf.int8
78	    converter.inference_output_type = tf.int8
79	
80	    def representative_dataset():
81	        for sample in representative:
82	            yield [sample[np.newaxis, ...].astype(np.float32)]
83	
84	    converter.representative_dataset = representative_dataset
85	    return converter.convert()

88	def tflite_predict(tflite_model: bytes, X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
89	    """Run the int8 interpreter sample by sample, returning float scores."""
90	    interpreter = tf.lite.Interpreter(model_content=tflite_model)
91	    interpreter.allocate_tensors()
92	    inp = interpreter.get_input_details()[0]
93	    out = interpreter.get_output_details()[0]
94	
95	    in_scale, in_zero = inp["quantization"]
96	    out_scale, out_zero = out["quantization"]
97	
98	    scores = np.empty(len(X), dtype=np.float32)
99	    for i, sample in enumerate(X):
100	        quantized = np.clip(
101	            np.round(sample / in_scale + in_zero), -128, 127
102	        ).astype(np.int8)
103	        interpreter.set_tensor(inp["index"], quantized[np.newaxis, ...])
104	        interpreter.invoke()
105	        raw = interpreter.get_tensor(out["index"])[0, 0]
106	        scores[i] = (float(raw) - out_zero) * out_scale
107	    return scores

110	def largest_activation_bytes(tflite_model: bytes) -> int:
111	    """Biggest intermediate tensor, as an int8 arena sanity check.
112	
113	    Not the arena size itself -- TFLM's real requirement depends on its
114	    allocation planner and has to be confirmed on device -- but this is the
115	    number that decides internal SRAM vs PSRAM.
116	    """
117	    interpreter = tf.lite.Interpreter(model_content=tflite_model)
118	    interpreter.allocate_tensors()
119	    return max(
120	        int(np.prod(d["shape"])) * np.dtype(d["dtype"]).itemsize
121	        for d in interpreter.get_tensor_details()
122	        if len(d["shape"]) > 0
123	    )

126	def write_c_array(data: bytes, path: Path, var_name: str) -> None:
127	    """Emit an xxd-style C array plus its header, for the firmware build.
128	
129	    The array is 16-byte aligned because TFLM requires the flatbuffer to be
130	    aligned before it will parse it in place.
131	    """
132	    lines = [
133	        "// Generated by src/export_tflite.py -- do not edit.",
134	        "//",
135	        f"// int8 doorbell classifier, {len(data)} bytes.",
136	        "",
137	        f'#include "{path.with_suffix(".h").name}"',
138	        "",
139	        f"alignas(16) const unsigned char {var_name}[] = {{",
140	    ]
141	    for offset in range(0, len(data), 12):
142	        chunk = ", ".join(f"0x{byte:02x}" for byte in data[offset : offset + 12])
143	        lines.append(f"    {chunk},")
144	    lines.append("};")
145	    lines.append(f"const unsigned int {var_name}_len = {len(data)};")
146	    lines.append("")
147	    path.write_text("\n".join(lines))
148	
149	    guard = path.with_suffix(".h").name.upper().replace(".", "_") + "_"
150	    path.with_suffix(".h").write_text(
151	        "\n".join(
152	            [
153	                "// Generated by src/export_tflite.py -- do not edit.",
154	                "",
155	                f"#ifndef {guard}",
156	                f"#define {guard}",
157	                "",
158	                f"extern const unsigned char {var_name}[];",
159	                f"extern const unsigned int {var_name}_len;",
160	                "",
161	                f"#endif  // {guard}",

1	# Doorbell Detector — Project Guide
2	
3	## What This Is
4	
5	Audio-based doorbell detection system running on a Raspberry Pi. The project has two
6	main modes: an ML-based collector (`data_collection/data_collector.py`) and a
7	pattern-matching detector (`data_collection/detector.py`), deployed as a systemd
8	service. Alongside the Pi scripts lives a DVC-managed ML pipeline (`src/`, `dvc.yaml`)
9	that pulls labels from Label Studio and raw audio from a self-hosted MinIO S3 bucket
10	to train an XGBoost bell classifier.
11	
12	## ML Data Pipeline (DVC)
13	
14	`uv run dvc repro` runs the full chain:
15	`fetch_labeled_data` (Label Studio CSV export) → `convert_labeled_data` →
16	`download_audio` (S3) → `extract_data_quality` / `augmentation` (SNR-mixed synthetic
17	`front_doorbell` samples) → `select_chunks` (chunking + balancing) →
18	`extract_features` → `draw_data` (slicing) → `train_model` (MLflow) →
19	`export_model` (int8 TFLite).
20	
21	- **A feature/model variant is a parameter, not a branch.** `feature_extraction.type`
22	  picks an entry in `src/features.py` (`mfcc`, `logmel`, `stft`, `yamnet`) which owns
23	  both the transform and the matching chunk slicer; `training.head` picks `cnn` or
24	  `xgboost`. Sweep with `dvc exp run -S`, not by forking dvc.yaml. Historic branches
25	  (`cnn-mfcc`, `cnn-spectrogram`, `yamnet-features`, `stft-spectrogram-features`,
26	  `cnn-logmel`, `esp32-logmel`) each hard-coded one combination; they are superseded.
27	- **`select_chunks` is deliberately feature-independent.** It decides which chunks make
28	  up the dataset and in what order, writes `data/chunk_manifest.csv`, and takes no
29	  `feature_extraction` param — so every variant trains on exactly the same chunks and
30	  reuses this stage's cache. `extract_features` is downstream of it and touches only
31	  the files the manifest references (1205 of 2801, and the difference is ~500 MB on the
32	  STFT variant). Anything that changes *which* chunks exist belongs in this stage.
33	- **`feature_extraction.features_dir` must be distinct per geometry.**
34	  `extract_features.py` stamps a `feature_config.json` into the directory and
35	  `draw_data.py` refuses to slice arrays whose stamp disagrees with `params.yaml`. This
36	  is the guard for the failure that produced `data/logmel_data.esp32bak`: two branches
37	  wrote different geometry (13 bands @ hop 512 vs 40 @ hop 320) into one directory name.
38	- **Hyperparameters are per head** (`model.cnn`, `model.xgboost`). A flat block
39	  meant XGBoost silently received the CNN's `learning_rate: 0.001` plus
40	  `dropout`/`epochs` as unknown kwargs and barely trained. Whether a representation
41	  needs log-compression before normalization is likewise a `FeatureSpec` property
42	  (`needs_log_compression`, true only for `stft`), not a params flag to remember.
43	- **`export_model` runs for every variant**, so candidates are ranked on their
44	  post-quantization score rather than their float32 one; `export.max_f1_drop` fails the
45	  stage on quantization collapse. Non-`cnn` heads write `models/export/SKIPPED.json`
46	  instead of a model.
47	
48	- **Storage layout:** bucket `doorbell-detector` on MinIO — `raw/` (audio, Label Studio
49	  source storage), `annotations/` (Label Studio target-storage sync, backup only),
50	  `dvc/` (DVC remote, configured in `.dvc/config`).
51	- **Credentials** live in the git-ignored `.env`: `LABEL_STUDIO_URL`,
52	  `LABEL_STUDIO_API_KEY`, `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`,
53	  `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI`, `MLFLOW_TRACKING_USERNAME`,
54	  `MLFLOW_TRACKING_PASSWORD`. Source it before `dvc repro`/`dvc push`.
55	- **Experiment tracking:** `train_xgboost.py` logs params/metrics/model/confusion-matrix
56	  to MLflow (experiment `doorbell-detector`) at `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` — a self-hosted
57	  server (`https://mlflow.saadeh.dev`), not managed from this repo. `dvc metrics
58	  show`/`dvc plots diff` no longer cover training metrics; check the MLflow UI instead.
59	  Runs are named `<head>-<feature_type>-<git_branch>` (feature type auto-detected from
60	  the `*_features` column in `balanced_data.h5`) and log `balanced_data_md5` — the md5
61	  DVC records for the dataset — so every run traces to an exact, `dvc pull`-able
62	  dataset version.
63	- **Label Studio auth** is a JWT personal access token: `fetch_data.sh` exchanges it
64	  via `/api/token/refresh` for a Bearer token (legacy `Token` header returns 401).
65	- **Incrementality:** `data/audio` is a `persist: true` output — unchanged labels skip
66	  the download stage entirely; changed labels download only missing files and prune
67	  removed ones. Labels are only re-fetched explicitly:
68	  `uv run dvc repro -f fetch_labeled_data && uv run dvc repro`.
69	- **Labeling convention:** bell events get span labels (e.g. `front_doorbell`);
70	  tag-only annotations (doorslam, voice, silence, …) have an empty `label` column in
71	  the export and become full-file `background` rows in the converter. The end time is
72	  filled with the real file duration in `select_chunks.py`.
73	- `convert_labeled_data.py` normalizes any Label Studio audio reference (plain
74	  `s3://`, presigned URL, resolver path) to canonical `s3://bucket/key` so presigned
75	  URL churn never dirties the pipeline.
76	- `features.py::_load_mono_int16_scale` downmixes to mono — stereo uploads would
77	  silently double the frame rate and break chunking. Audio is kept at int16 amplitude
78	  scale (not [-1, 1]); normalization happens globally at training time.
79	- Requires `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` on the host (pydub `mediainfo`).
80	- **Augmentation (`augment_data.py`):** grows the minority `front_doorbell` class by
81	  mixing real doorbell chunks (signal) with real background chunks (noise) via simple
82	  addition at each `augmentation.snrs_db` target SNR (`params.yaml`; `flat_doorbell` is
83	  excluded — too little raw data to seed it). Each signal chunk is paired with
84	  `pairs_per_signal_chunk` random noise chunks per SNR; the noise is circularly
85	  time-shifted and each mix gets ±`gain_jitter_db` uniform loudness jitter. Rows carry
86	  `split_group` = source file of the signal chunk (leakage guard, see training note
87	  below). Output rows carry `end = (chunk_size +
88	  1) / 1000`, 1ms past the real chunk length; this is a deliberate metadata trick so
89	  `select_chunks.py`'s sliding-window loop emits exactly one `chunk_start=0` window per
90	  augmented file, reusing the real-annotation chunking path unmodified.
91	- `fixed_rate_slice` in `features.py` slices chunks using a **fixed**
92	  `sample_rate/hop_length` frame rate, not `array.shape[1] / file_duration`. The latter
93	  is biased by librosa's constant `+1` frame-count offset — negligible for long real
94	  files (always rounded to the same width) but dominant for exactly `chunk_size`-long
95	  augmented clips (rounded to a different width), which broke `np.vstack` in
96	  `train_xgboost.py` once augmented and real chunks were trained together. `yamnet` is
97	  the exception: it mean-pools the covering frames instead, because a 2s augmented clip
98	  yields 3 embedding frames where a 2s slice of a long file yields 4. That pooling
99	  removes the time axis, so `yamnet` only works with the `xgboost` head —
100	  `train_model.py` enforces it.
101	- **Train/val split is group-aware** (`prepare_split` in `train_cnn.py`): `StratifiedGroupKFold`
102	  grouped by `split_group` (source recording; augmented rows inherit their signal
103	  chunk's source file). A plain random chunk split leaks near-duplicate overlapping
104	  windows and SNR variants across the split and inflates validation metrics.
105	  `training.test_size` maps to the fold fraction (1/n_splits); the realized fraction
106	  is logged to MLflow as `realized_test_fraction`.
107	
108	## GSD Workflow
109	
110	This project uses [Get Shit Done](https://github.com/amjadsaadeh/gsd) for structured
111	planning and execution.
112	
113	**Status:** v1.0 milestone complete — all 3 phases shipped 2026-06-25. Post-milestone
114	hardening (MQTT trigger fixes, audio drop fixes, template auto-trim) has continued

cd /home/orchid/projects/doorbell-detector
export PYTHONPATH=./src:.
git add -- params.yaml dvc.yaml dvc.lock CLAUDE.md src/ tests/ models/tflite_metrics.json
git commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
give each training head its own hyperparameter block

Unifying the two trainers behind one `model:` block silently broke the
xgboost head: XGBClassifier received the CNN's learning_rate (0.001, against
xgboost's default estimator count) plus dropout/epochs/early_stopping_patience
as unknown kwargs. It barely trained. The yamnet variant is the only one that
requires that head, and it came back at val F1 0.000 / train F1 0.399 -- an
impossible number, which is the only reason this was caught. With
model.cnn / model.xgboost split, the same variant scores 0.986.

While here, move log-compression out of params entirely. Whether a
representation needs np.log before normalization is a fact about the
representation -- raw STFT magnitudes span orders of magnitude, mfcc and
logmel already had a log applied by the extractor, and yamnet embeddings go
negative so logging them would produce NaN. It is now a FeatureSpec field
(needs_log_compression, true only for stft) instead of a params flag whose
comment said "flip this on the spectrogram branch".

random_state likewise moves to training, since the split and both heads share it.

Adds regression tests asserting the blocks do not leak each other's
hyperparameters and that stft is the only type wanting log compression.

content.text:
Done. Here's the report.

## What shipped

Two commits on a new branch `unified-pipeline` (off `cnn-logmel`), all five recommendations implemented and verified.

**1 + 2. Branch-per-variant collapsed into parameters.** `src/features.py` is now a registry keyed by `feature_extraction.type` where each entry owns *both* the transform and its matching chunk slicer — the two halves that had been drifting apart across branches (each branch hand-edited its own slicer inside `draw_data.py`). `src/train_model.py` dispatches on `training.head`. `dvc.yaml` interpolates `${feature_extraction.features_dir}`. A variant is now `dvc exp run -S`, not a fork. Four extractor scripts became one; `extract_mfcc_features.py` and `extract_logmel_features.py` are deleted.

The `.esp32bak` failure mode is now guarded: `extract_features` stamps a `feature_config.json` into the features directory and `draw_data` refuses to slice arrays whose stamp disagrees with `params.yaml`.

**3. Noise pruning — bigger than I estimated.** Splitting `select_chunks` out of `draw_data` puts sampling *upstream* of extraction, so it touches **1205 files instead of 2801** (57% fewer). It also makes sampling feature-independent, so all variants share one cached stage and train on identical chunks. Verified byte-identical: the manifest reproduces the previous `balanced_data.h5` row for row, in order.

**4. `export_model` promoted** into the default DAG, so variants are ranked post-quantization. Non-CNN heads write a skip marker.

Tests: **44 → 101**.

## Leaderboard, all on the same 1770-chunk manifest

| Variant | Head | Input | val F1 | int8 F1 | Peak activation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| logmel 40 mel / 320 hop | cnn | (40, 100, 1) | **1.0000** | 1.0000 | 125 KB |
| mfcc 40 coef / 320 hop | cnn | (40, 100, 1) | **1.0000** | 1.0000 | 125 KB |
| stft 256 fft / 128 hop | cnn | (129, 250, 1) | 0.9973 | 0.9973 | **1008 KB** |
| logmel 13 mel / 512 hop | cnn | (13, 62, 1) | 0.9973 | — | — |
| yamnet | xgboost | 1024 | 0.9862 | skipped | — |

**The -15 dB sweep did not break the ceiling.** It only separates variants at 13 bands. At the 40-band geometry you actually deploy, log-mel and MFCC both sit at exactly 1.0 and are indistinguishable. The real limiter is the val fold: 183 chunks, so one flipped label is 0.0027. Before trusting any ranking here, I'd switch to averaging all `StratifiedGroupKFold` folds rather than taking `next()` on the first — that's a small change to `prepare_split` and it costs nothing but runtime.

The STFT number is the one that matters for the ESP32 decision: it ties on accuracy while needing **8× the SRAM**.

## Two bugs I introduced, and one I found

**I committed 769 MB into git.** `git add -A` swept in `data/stft_data/`, which `data/.gitignore` never covered. `.git` went 17 MB → 786 MB. Rewritten out, refs cleaned, back to **17 MB**; `/stft_data` and `/features` now ignored. I should have staged explicitly.

**`dvc exp run` left HEAD detached and staged its mutated `params.yaml`.** My "clean" recommit landed off-branch and captured `type: yamnet, head: xgboost` as the repo default. Fixed. Practical lesson now in `CLAUDE.md`: use `dvc exp run --temp`, which touches neither.

**The unification silently broke the XGBoost head.** One flat `model:` block fed both trainers, so `XGBClassifier` got the CNN's `learning_rate: 0.001` plus `dropout`/`epochs` as unknown kwargs and barely trained. YAMNet came back at val F1 **0.000** — the only reason I caught it. Split into `model.cnn` / `model.xgboost`, and that variant now scores **0.9862**. I also moved log-compression out of params entirely: it's a fact about the representation (`needs_log_compression`, true only for `stft`), not a flag whose comment said "flip this on the spectrogram branch".

That bug is a fair argument that the flat block was under-tested before I ran a variant through it — there are now regression tests asserting the blocks don't leak each other's hyperparameters.

## Open items

- `data/logmel_data.esp32bak` (98 MB) is still on disk and now redundant. Yours to delete: `rm -rf data/logmel_data.esp32bak`.
- MLflow run names show `-HEAD` for `dvc exp` runs because those execute detached. Cosmetic, but `get_git_branch()` should prefer `DVC_EXP_NAME`.
- Nothing pushed — branch is local, and `dvc push` hasn't run, so the new feature dirs and models aren't on MinIO yet.
- The six superseded experiment branches are untouched. `CLAUDE.md` marks them superseded rather than deleting them.
